answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated, time-separated work that independent peers verify and that later proves useful, such as completing orchard maintenance tasks or routing a raven’s alert through a wharf network. A new identity starts with no track record, and work is sampled for review; copying identities does not multiply verified history. An attacker must therefore fund many agents, keep them active, and produce useful work long enough to build trust, making a cheap burst of fake accounts ineffective.
